subject: ventures/tile-layout-optimizer
professional: a senior tile setter / flooring estimator (CTI-level installer) who orders tile by the box and plans layouts; first checks: does the count match a hand layout, are cut positions measured from the wall, are cuts physically possible with a saw kerf, and does the recommended bond respect the ANSI A108.02 offset limit for large-format tile

evidence.correctness: Ran it. Independent brute force (/tmp/claude-0/audit-tile-layout-optimizer/brute.mjs, my own 0.1 mm offset sweep per axis, no subject logic) vs optimizeTile on 40 random straight-grid, no-reuse rooms with and without a 50 mm min cut: {agree: 40, worse: 0, better: 0}, so the offset search reaches the true optimum on these. Hand cutting-stock cases (hand.mjs): 75x60 cm room, 30 cm tiles: kerf 0 -> 5 (two 150 mm strips share a tile), kerf 2 mm -> 6 (150+2+150 > 300); 90x60 room, 60x30 half bond: 3 / 4; all match and verifyPlan ok. Rule of thumb and purchase recomputed by hand for the sample: floor (3650x5100 - 1690x1490 mm) = 16.0969 m2; plank 16.0969/0.244209*1.1 -> 73, 13 boxes, $806; large 49; subway 97; best plank 67 *1.05 -> 71 -> 12 boxes $744; imperial 12x12 ft, 12 in tile, 1/8 in grout -> 156 both. All guide-page figures (67/66/73/82/$744/$806/$930, 46 tiles) reproduce. Capped at 3: offcut packing optimality is heuristic and unproven beyond the lower bound.
evidence.completeness: node --test: 40/40 pass in 4.7 s. Claimed features exercised (csv.mjs, sample.mjs): layout search over start/orientation/bond, cut-outs (L-shape sample), several tile options ranked by box cost, rule-of-thumb and corner-start comparison, cutting list CSV, metric and imperial, parseTiles paste, independent verifier run before display (index.html:366). Drawing checked only by page.test.mjs element/import checks, not rendered in a browser. No stubs or TODOs found.
evidence.verification: node --test 40/40 pass. Mutations via quality_mutate.py: 1 of 5 caught. Survivors: dropping the saw kerf in one guillotine split branch (calc.mjs:267) - my own random harness (mutcase2.mjs) shows that mutant yields verifier-rejected plans in 25 of 150 random rooms, yet the suite's 40-room random test misses it; changing the brick shift denominator (calc.mjs:169) - verifyPlan reuses the same shiftOf, and the only brick test asserts tiles >= 4; minCut boundary < -> <=; rule-of-thumb grout removal. Only purchase Math.ceil->round was caught.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (702 lines) fully, test files, index.html script head. Integer hundredths-of-mm geometry, clean rect subtraction, seeded deterministic packer, verifier is a genuinely separate coverage sweep over compressed coordinates. Weak spots: verifier imports the same shiftOf as the generator (not independent for bond geometry); positions reported relative to the expansion-gap line but labelled 'from the wall'; inline page script not unit-tested beyond lookups.
evidence.claims: Checked: guide worked-example numbers (reproduce exactly, sample.mjs); 'nothing uploaded' (page.test.mjs network check passes, no fetch in calc.mjs); lower bound shown (evaluate returns lowerBound); 'independent checker re-verifies every plan' (index.html:366, true, though bond geometry is shared); disclaimer present on both pages; limits listed (no herringbone/diagonal, out-of-square). Mismatch: index.html:390 says rule of thumb is 'floor area over tile area' but calc.mjs:449 divides by pitch area (tile+grout), giving 73 vs 74 for the sample plank. Served llms.txt uses marisstella.app (served-copy.mjs: no placeholder origins).
evidence.fitness: Walked the job: enter an L-shaped room and three tiles, get a ranked box/cost table, a start line and a CSV cutting list (39 cut rows for the sample plank). A tiler could order from it with own spare. Gaps on site: start line and cut positions are measured from the gap line, not the wall (10 mm off in the sample); packer ignores which edge of an offcut is factory vs cut, so a reused piece can put a cut edge against a grout joint; no warning when a half bond is chosen for tile over 18 in.
evidence.domain: Compared against ANSI A108.02 sec. 4.3.8 / TCNA Handbook guidance: for running-bond tile with the offset side longer than 18 in (457 mm), offset should not exceed 33% unless the manufacturer says otherwise, because tile bow turns into lippage at a half offset. The tool offers and recommends a half bond with no warning: sample subway-size 30x60 cm (24 in) best layout is 'half' (sample.mjs), and the guide (how-to-lay-tile-with-less-waste.html:35) and FAQ (index.html:180) say a half offset 'hides' bow, which is the opposite of the standard. Grout pitch, kerf, min cut (50 mm / one-third convention) and expansion gap are modelled correctly.

mod(j * bond.num, bond.den) -> mod(j * bond.num, bond.den + 1) in shiftOf
if (d < p.minCut) slivers++; -> if (d <= p.minCut) slivers++;

defects.what: Half-offset brick bond is offered and recommended for tile with a side over 18 in (sample 30x60 cm best = half bond) with no warning, against ANSI A108.02 4.3.8 / TCNA guidance of max 33% offset; the guide and FAQ say a half offset hides bow, the opposite of the standard
Dropping the saw kerf in one guillotine split branch survives the suite although it makes 17% of random rooms produce plans the verifier rejects; the 40-room random test is too small/narrow to hit it
Brick-bond row shift is unchecked: verifyPlan imports the same shiftOf as the generator and the only brick test asserts tiles >= 4, so a wrong shift survives
Start line and cutting-list positions are measured from the expansion-gap line but labelled 'from the left/back wall' (off by the wall gap, 10 mm in the sample)
Page says the rule of thumb is floor area over tile area; code divides by tile+grout pitch area (sample plank 73 vs 74)
Offcut packer does not track factory vs cut edges, so a reused piece can place a cut edge against a visible grout joint

verdict: A careful, correct layout engine: an independent brute-force sweep matched its straight-grid optimum on 40 of 40 random rooms, hand cutting-stock cases with and without kerf matched, and every worked-example figure reproduces. It misses the bar on verification (1 of 5 seeded mutants caught; a kerf bug that breaks 17% of random plans survives, and the verifier shares the bond geometry it should check) and falls short on domain because it recommends half-offset bond for 24 in tile without the ANSI A108.02 33% warning and tells readers a half offset hides bow. Finished, not yet expert-grade.
